classification.difficultyReason: Match function and derivative graphs by coordinating slope signs, stationary-point zeros and steepening or flattening near asymptotes.

inlines.text: The following are the graphs of

spec.description: Horizontal derivative graph coincident with the x-axis, with arrows both ways.
Increasing straight line through the origin with arrows at both ends.
spec.mathematics: Derivative changes from negative to positive at the origin.

spec.description: Upward-opening parabola with two x-intercepts and a minimum below the x-axis.
spec.mathematics: Derivative sign is positive, then negative, then positive.

spec.description: Increasing curve below the x-axis, approaching it from below to the right.
spec.mathematics: Derivative remains negative and approaches zero from below.

spec.description: Two negative branches descending without bound near x=0 and approaching y=0 from below away from the y-axis.
spec.mathematics: Derivative is negative on both sides of an undefined point.

spec.description: Positive left branch and negative right branch, with vertical asymptote x=0 and horizontal asymptote y=0.
spec.mathematics: Derivative has opposite signs on the two sides of x=0.

spec.description: Two-branch hyperbola in quadrants I and III, approaching both axes.
spec.mathematics: Positive right branch, negative left branch; f decreases on both sides of x=0.

answer.worked: The graph decreases on both sides of $x=0$, so $f'(x)<0$ on both branches. Its slope becomes steep near the vertical asymptote and tends to zero away from it. Hence (V).

spec.description: Rising cubic with a local maximum, a local minimum and three x-intercepts.
spec.mathematics: Gradient is positive, then negative, then positive.

answer.worked: The two turning points give two zeros of $f'$. The cubic increases, decreases, then increases, so $f'$ is positive, negative, then positive. Hence (III).

spec.description: Upward-opening parabola with its vertex at the origin.
spec.mathematics: Negative gradient left of the vertex, zero at it, positive gradient right of it.

answer.worked: The parabola decreases to its vertex, then increases. Its gradient changes from negative through zero to positive, as in (II).
A horizontal line has gradient zero everywhere, so its derivative is the x-axis, (I).

spec.description: Positive branches on both sides of x=0, rising without bound near it and approaching the x-axis away from it.
spec.mathematics: Original increases on the left branch and decreases on the right branch.

answer.worked: The left branch increases, so $f'>0$ there; the right branch decreases, so $f'<0$ there. The slopes become steep near $x=0$ and flatten away from it. Hence (VI).

spec.description: Decreasing curve above the x-axis, flattening towards it to the right.
spec.mathematics: Derivative is negative but approaches zero from below.

answer.worked: The graph decreases throughout and flattens to the right. Thus $f'$ stays negative and approaches zero from below, as in (IV).
